{{short description|Italian physicist (born 1955)}}
[[File:Antonio Ereditato, 2015 (cropped).jpg|thumb|Ereditato in 2015]]

'''Antonio Ereditato''' (born 2 June 1955) is an [[Italians|Italian]] [[physicist]].<ref name="science.org">{{cite journal |title=Leaders of Faster-Than-Light Experiment Step Down |url=https://www.science.org/content/article/leaders-faster-light-experiment-step-down |journal=Science |doi=10.1126/article.27546 |doi-broken-date=15 June 2026 }}</ref> He is a Visiting Professor at the [[University of Chicago]], associate researcher at [[Fermilab]], [[Batavia, New York|Batavia]], [[United States]], and Emeritus professor at the [[University of Bern]], [[Switzerland]], where he has been Director of the Laboratory for High Energy Physics from 2006 to 2020.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=cern |date=2020-05-18 |title=A first taste of neutrino physics |url=https://cerncourier.com/a/a-first-taste-of-neutrino-physics/ |access-date=2026-05-15 |website=CERN Courier |language=en-US}}</ref> From 2021 to 2022 Ereditato has been Visiting Professor at the [[Yale University]], United States.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=Ereditato joins Yale Physics as Visiting Professor {{!}} Department of Physics |url=https://physics.yale.edu/news/ereditato-joins-yale-physics-visiting-professor |access-date=2026-05-15 |website=physics.yale.edu}}</ref>

He carried out research activities in the field of experimental [[neutrino]] physics,<ref>{{Citation |last=Ereditato |first=Antonio |chapter=Front matter |date=2017 |title=The State of the Art of Neutrino Physics |volume=28 |issue= |pages=i–viii |chapter-url=https://www.worldscientific.com/doi/abs/10.1142/9789813226098_fmatter |access-date=2026-05-15 |series=Advanced Series on Directions in High Energy Physics |publisher=WORLD SCIENTIFIC |doi=10.1142/9789813226098_fmatter |isbn=978-981-322-608-1|chapter-url-access=subscription }}</ref> of [[weak interactions]] and [[strong interactions]] with experiments conducted at [[CERN]], in [[Japan]], at [[Fermi National Accelerator Laboratory|Fermilab]] in [[United States]] and at the [[LNGS]] in Italy.<ref>{{Cite news |title=A strength test for the strong force |url=https://www.symmetrymagazine.org/article/a-strength-test-for-the-strong-force?language_content_entity=und |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260326220357/https://www.symmetrymagazine.org/article/a-strength-test-for-the-strong-force?language_content_entity=und |archive-date=2026-03-26 |access-date=2026-05-15 |work=symmetry magazine |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2004-09-05 |title=The high-intensity frontier |url=https://cerncourier.com/a/the-high-intensity-frontier/ |access-date=2026-05-15 |website=CERN Courier |language=en-US}}</ref> Ereditato has accomplished several R&D studies on particle detectors: wire chambers, calorimeters, time projection chambers, [[nuclear emulsion]]s, detectors for medical applications.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2010-06-02 |title=Double celebration for neutrino lab |url=https://physicsworld.com/double-celebration-for-neutrino-lab/ |access-date=2026-05-15 |website=Physics World |language=en-GB}}</ref>

==Biography==
Ereditato was born on 2 June 1955 in [[Naples]]. He obtained the degree in physics (1981) and the PhD (1987) at the [[University of Naples Federico II]]. He worked at CNRS Strasbourg, at [[CERN]] and at the [[Istituto Nazionale di Fisica Nucleare]] in Naples, where he obtained the position of Director of Research since 1998. From 2006 to 2020 Ereditato has been Ordinary Professor of Experimental Particle Physics at the [[University of Bern]].<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |title=Fermilab and the University of Bern join forces for neutrino research |url=https://www.jahresbericht2019.unibe.ch/key_areas/matter_and_the_universe/fermilab/index_eng.html |access-date=2026-05-15 |website=www.jahresbericht2019.unibe.ch}}</ref>

He has served in several international scientific committees: SPSC, CNGS and LHCC at [[CERN]], and is presently member of the PAC of the [[Joint Institute for Nuclear Research]] of Dubna. Ereditato has been also member of the [[Swiss National Science Foundation]]. He served in Advisory Committees of international conferences, such as the Calorimetry Conference. Referee and peer review member of international journals and of Funding Agencies, Ereditato is currently Editor-in-Chief of Instruments.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.mdpi.com/journal/instruments|title=Instruments}}</ref> He is also member of the Aspen Institute Italia<ref>[https://www.aspeninstitute.it/ Aspen Institute Italia]</ref>{{Better source needed|reason=This is just an institution homepage.|date=January 2021}} and has been president of SAIS (Association of the Italian Academics in Switzerland).<ref>[https://www.saisitalia.ch/ SAIS]</ref>{{Better source needed|reason=This is just an institution homepage.|date=January 2021}}

From 2008 to 2012 Antonio Ereditato has been the spokesperson of the [[OPERA]] neutrino experiment that he proposed in 1997 together with Kimio Niwa and Paolo Strolin. The experiment studied [[neutrino oscillations]] along the CNGS beam from CERN to the LNGS [[Gran Sasso Laboratory]]. On 31 May 2010 Ereditato announced the detection of the first [[tau-neutrino]] by OPERA. This was the first indication of the direct appearance of neutrino oscillations. In September 2011 the [[OPERA]] Collaboration announced that an anomaly was detected in the measurement of the neutrino velocity, pointing to the possibility of superluminal muon neutrinos, see (mistaken) [[faster-than-light neutrino anomaly]]. The source of the anomaly was then found by the OPERA researchers as due to an instrumental problem.<ref name="JHEP10 2012">{{Cite journal |last1=Adam |first1=T. |last2=Adam |first2=T. |last3=Agafonova |first3=N. |last4=Aleksandrov |first4=A. |last5=Altinok |first5=O. |last6=Alvarez Sanchez |first6=P. |last7=Anokhina |first7=A. |last8=Aoki |first8=S. |last9=Ariga |first9=A. |last10=Ariga |first10=T. |last11=Autiero |first11=D. |last12=Badertscher |first12=A. |last13=Ben Dhahbi |first13=A. |last14=Bertolin |first14=A. |last15=Bozza |first15=C. |last16=Brugière |first16=T. |last17=Brugnera |first17=R. |last18=Brunet |first18=F. |last19=Brunetti |first19=G. |last20=Buontempo |first20=S. |last21=Carlus |first21=B. |last22=Cavanna |first22=F. |last23=Cazes |first23=A. |last24=Chaussard |first24=L. |last25=Chernyavsky |first25=M. |last26=Chiarella |first26=V. |last27=Chukanov |first27=A. |last28=Colosimo |first28=G. |last29=Crespi |first29=M. |last30=D'Ambrosio |first30=N. |display-authors=1 |title=Measurement of the neutrino velocity with the OPERA detector in the CNGS beam |journal=Journal of High Energy Physics |date=2012 |issue=10 |article-number=93 |arxiv = 1109.4897 |doi=10.1007/JHEP10(2012)093 |bibcode=2012JHEP...10..093A}}</ref>

As head of the [[ATLAS experiment|ATLAS]] Bern group, Ereditato contributed to the discovery of the [[Higgs Boson]] in 2012.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://inspirehep.net/record/1124337|title=Inspire}}</ref> In the framework of the [[T2K]] experiment in Japan, in 2013 he took part in the discovery of the appearance of neutrino oscillations <ref name=Abe>{{Cite journal | last1=Abe | first1=K. | last2=Adam | first2=J. | last3=Aihara | first3=H. | last4=Akiri | first4=T. | last5=Andreopoulos | first5=C. | last6=Aoki | first6=S. | last7=Ariga | first7=A. | last8=Ariga | first8=T. | last9=Assylbekov | first9=S. | last10=Autiero | first10=D. | last11=Barbi | first11=M. | last12=Barker | first12=G. J. | last13=Barr | first13=G. | last14=Bass | first14=M. | last15=Batkiewicz | first15=M. | last16=Bay | first16=F. | last17=Bentham | first17=S. W. | last18=Berardi | first18=V. | last19=Berger | first19=B. E. | last20=Berkman | first20=S. | last21=Bertram | first21=I. | last22=Bhadra | first22=S. | last23=Blaszczyk | first23=F. d. He is involved in the United States neutrino program. He has been one of the founders of the [[Deep Underground Neutrino Experiment|DUNE]] experiment for the high precision study of neutrino oscillations and astroparticle physics. Ereditato's group contributed to the realization of the Near Detector of the experiment with the so-called ArgonCube liquid argon time projection chamber.

==Scientific achievements==
Ereditato is known for contributions to [[neutrino physics]], [[calorimetry]], and detector development.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2015-05-06 |title=The Data That Threatened to Break Physics - Nautilus |url=https://nautil.us/the-data-that-threatened-to-break-physics-235415/ |access-date=2026-05-15 |website=nautil.us |language=en}}</ref> His early work at [[CERN]] included leading trigger and [[calorimeter]] studies in the NA10 experiment and CHARM II, contributing to precision electroweak measurements.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2012-03-30 |title=Neutrino 'faster than light' scientist resigns |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/science-environment-17560379 |access-date=2026-05-15 |work=BBC News |language=en-GB}}</ref>

He played a key role in calorimeter R&D through the SPACAL project and co-founded the CALOR Conference. He proposed and led detector innovations for the CHORUS experiment, established leading short-baseline neutrino oscillation limits, and was a co-originator of the OPERA experiment, which achieved the first direct observation of ντ appearance.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Antonio Ereditato {{!}} Yale High Energy Physics |url=https://hep.yale.edu/people/antonio-ereditato |access-date=2026-05-15 |website=hep.yale.edu}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Dacey |first=James |date=2012-08-28 |title=Lessons learned by leading OPERA man |url=https://physicsworld.com/a/lessons-learned-by-leading-opera-man/ |access-date=2026-05-15 |website=Physics World |language=en-GB}}</ref>

At the Laboratory for [[High Energy Physics]], he expanded programs in [[neutrino physics]], antimatter studies, and medical applications, contributing to milestone results including the first indication of nonzero θ13 and νe appearance in T2K experiment and the discovery of the [[Higgs boson]] with [[ATLAS experiment]].<ref name=":0" /> He also pioneered liquid argon detector advances through ARGONTUBE, [[MicroBooNE]], and DUNE, and contributed to antimatter interferometry through AEgIS experiment and QUPLAS.<ref name=YalePhysics>{{Cite web |title=Yale Physics Wright Lab researchers developing new neutrino detector technologies {{!}} Department of Physics |url=https://physics.yale.edu/news/yale-physics-wright-lab-researchers-developing-new-neutrino-detector-technologies |access-date=2026-05-15 |website=physics.yale.edu}}</ref>

As full professor of experimental particle physics at the [[University of Bern]] from 2006 to 2020, Ereditato transformed Bern into a major international center for [[neutrino]] and [[Sensor|detector physics]].<ref name=":2" /> He directed the Laboratory for [[High Energy Physics]],<ref name=":0" /> co-directed the Physics Institute, and later served as director of the Albert Einstein Center for Fundamental Physics and deputy dean of the Faculty of Science.<ref name=":1" /> Under his leadership Bern became deeply involved in major international collaborations including ATLAS Collaboration, T2K Collaboration, [[MicroBooNE]], SBND, and DUNE.<ref name=":0" /> His work contributed to the discovery of the [[Higgs boson]] at [[CERN]], the first evidence for nonzero θ<sub>13</sub> neutrino mixing, the discovery of electron-neutrino appearance, measurements of muon-antineutrino disappearance, and hints for [[CP violation]] in neutrino oscillation.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Lewis |first=Renee |title=The mystery of the Higgs boson |url=https://www.aljazeera.com/features/2012/1/9/the-mystery-of-the-higgs-boson |access-date=2026-06-15 |website=Al Jazeera |language=en}}</ref>

A major focus of Ereditato's later career has been innovation in liquid-argon time projection chamber technology. His ARGONTUBE detector achieved world-record drift-track lengths in liquid argon and pioneered ultraviolet laser calibration methods that became foundational for next-generation neutrino observatories.<ref name=YalePhysics/> The Bern led ARGONCUBE project, produced the first proof-of-principle pixelated readout architecture for liquid-argon detectors and became central to detector design for the international DUNE experiment.<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Asaadi | first1=Jonathan | last2=Auger | first2=Martin | last3=Ereditato | first3=Antonio | last4=Goeldi | first4=Damian | last5=Kose | first5=Umut | last6=Kreslo | first6=Igor | last7=Lorca | first7=David | last8=Luethi | first8=Matthias | last9=Rudolf von Rohr | first9=Christoph | last10=Sinclair | first10=James | last11=Stocker | first11=Francesca | last12=Weber | first12=Michele | title=First Demonstration of a Pixelated Charge Readout for Single-Phase Liquid Argon Time Projection Chambers | journal=Instruments | date=2020 | volume=4 | page=9 | doi=10.3390/instruments4010009 | doi-access=free }}</ref> Ereditato's instrumentation work also extended into antimatter physics, contributing to the first observation of antimatter quantum interferometry through the QUPLAS program, as well as isotope-production systems for the Bern cyclotron laboratory with applications in nuclear medicine.<ref name=":1" />

Ereditato has held numerous institutional leadership roles across global physics governance, including service on [[CERN]]'s Large Hadron Collider Committee, CERN SPS Committee,<ref>{{Cite news |title='Unexpected results' at Cern |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/av/science-environment-15034426 |access-date=2026-06-15 |work=BBC News |language=en-GB}}</ref> the [[Swiss National Science Foundation]] Council, [[Fermilab]]'s International Executive Board for the Long Baseline Neutrino Facility, the [[U.S. Department of Energy]] International Neutrino Council, and advisory committees at [[Dubna]] and [[CERN]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2017-03-21 |title=Personal Page |url=https://www.lhep.unibe.ch/about_us/people/personal_page/index_eng.html |access-date=2026-06-15 |website=Laboratory for High Energy Physics (LHEP)}}</ref> He has also played influential editorial roles, serving on the boards of ''[[New Journal of Physics]]'' and ''[[Advances in High Energy Physics]]'', and as founding editor-in-chief of ''Instruments''.<ref name=":1" /> Ereditato is currently Faculty of the Collegio Europeo di Parma and Chairs the Scientific Committee of the Collegio La Sapienza  of the ONAOSI, in Perugia.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Mosconi |first=Franco |date=2022-06-24 |title=Una politica industriale per l'Europa |url=https://www.pandorarivista.it/articoli/una-politica-industriale-per-l-europa/ |access-date=2026-06-15 |website=Pandora Rivista |language=it-IT}}</ref>

His scholarly output includes more than 1,660 scientific papers, over 292,000 citations, and a [[Google Scholar]] h-index exceeding 230, placing him among the most highly cited experimental physicists of his generation. He has delivered more than forty invited international conference lectures and supervised dozens of doctoral researchers who have gone on to major careers in international science.<ref name="science.org"/>

Beyond technical scholarship, Ereditato is a science writer. His books—including ''Le Particelle Elementari'',<ref name="Ereditato 2017">{{Cite book |last=Ereditato |first=Antonio |title=Le particelle elementari |date=2017 |publisher=Il Saggiatore |isbn=978-88-428-2352-0 |series=La cultura |location=Milano}}</ref> ''Ever Smaller'',<ref name=":3">{{Cite book |last1=Ereditato |first1=Antonio |title=Ever smaller: nature's elementary particles, from the atom to the neutrino and beyond |last2=Segre |first2=Erica |last3=Carnell |first3=Simon |last4=Lockyer |first4=Nigel |date=2017 |publisher=The MIT Press |isbn=978-0-262-04386-1 |location=Cambridge, Massachusetts}}</ref> ''The State of the Art of Neutrino Physics'',<ref name=":0" /> ''Il Mio Neutrino'',<ref name=":4">{{cite book | last1=Ereditato | first1=Antonio | title=Il mio neutrino | date=2022 | publisher=Rubbettino | isbn=978-88-498-7247-7 }}</ref> ''Zitto e Calcola!'',<ref name=":5">{{cite book | last1=Ereditato | first1=Antonio | title=Zitto e calcola! Corso introduttivo di meccanica quantistica per studenti principianti ma curiosi | date=2023 | publisher=Eurilink | isbn=979-12-80164-56-8 }}</ref> ''Lettera agli Scienziati del Futuro''<ref>{{Cite web |title=Lettera agli scienziati del futuro |url=https://www.ilsaggiatore.com/libro/lettera-agli-scienziati-del-futuro |access-date=2026-06-15 |website=Il Saggiatore |language=it}}</ref>'', The New Nuclear Power,''<ref name=":6">{{cite book |last1=Buono |first1=Stefano |last2=Ereditato |first2=Antonio  |title=The New Nuclear Power: A Journey Through the Future of Energy |date=2025 |publisher=Bocconi University Press |location=Chicago |isbn=979-12-81627-61-1 |edition=1st}}</ref> ''Il Sarto e il Calzolaio di Boltzmann'' have helped make modern particle physics accessible to broader audiences.<ref name=":7">{{Cite web |last=Ereditato |first=Antonio |date=2026-04-09 |title=La fatica di capire {{!}} Perché la fisica non si può spiegare con frasi a effetto |url=https://www.linkiesta.it/2026/04/einstein-libro-egea-antonio-ereditato/ |access-date=2026-06-15 |website=Linkiesta.it |language=it-IT}}</ref>

== Awards and honors ==
His honors include the [[Italian Physical Society]] Young Researcher Prize (1985),<ref>{{Cite web |title=Antonio Ereditato {{!}} Yale High Energy Physics |url=https://hep.yale.edu/people/antonio-ereditato |access-date=2026-06-15 |website=hep.yale.edu}}</ref> the shared 2016 [[Breakthrough Prize in Fundamental Physics]] for the contributions to the discovery of [[neutrino oscillation]]s, the Premio Caccuri for Literature and Science (2017), the Maria Antonia Gervasio Prize for scientific communication (2017),<ref name=":1" /> appointment as [[Order of Merit of the Italian Republic|Officer of the Order of Merit of the Italian Republic]] (2018),<ref>{{Cite web |title=The Scientific Committee {{!}} Management Innovation |url=https://www.managementinnovation.it/en/the-scientific-committee/ |access-date=2026-06-15 |language=en-US}}</ref> honorary citizenship of Caccuri, the "I Numeri Uno" Prize of the Italian Chamber of Commerce for Switzerland (2021), the shared 2025 Breakthrough Prize in Fundamental Physics recognizing precision measurements and discoveries at the [[Large Hadron Collider]],<ref>{{Cite web |title=ATLAS Collaboration – 2025 Breakthrough Prize in Fundamental Physics |url=https://breakthroughprize.org/Laureates/1/L3993 |access-date=2026-06-15 |website=breakthroughprize.org |language=en}}</ref> the 2026 Premio Villa Buitoni for "Courageous Careers".<ref>{{Cite web |last=VivoGubbio |date=2026-06-05 |title=Premio Villa Buitoni - Carriere Coraggiose 2026: emozioni e prestigio |url=https://www.vivogubbio.com/premio-villa-buitoni-carriere-coraggiose-2026-emozioni-e-prestigio/ |access-date=2026-06-15 |website=Vivo Gubbio {{!}} News dal Territorio: Gubbio, Perugia e Umbria |language=it-IT}}</ref>
